newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS MONDAY WEAKER ON U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS MONDAY WEAKER ON U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar ended Monday's interbank session weaker against the key U.S. dollar on the back of continued import pressure coupled with a panic wave evoked by a Reserve Bank statement last Friday that the local unit was overvalued.
"We've seen a bit of volatility on the market especially after the governor's statement," one dealer commented.

"It (also) looks like the market is still very short. We saw orders (bids) as high as 11.65 (for U.S. dollars) and all banks are quoting wide spreads ranging from 10 to 20 points," another dealer said.
"No one can afford to lose U.S. dollars right now so they are all quoting high to protect their offer side," he added.

In an interview with the private-owned Financial Gazette newspaper published on Friday, Reserve Bank governor Leonard Tsumba said the Zimbabwe dollar was overvalued by five percent and hinted the bank would allow it to depreciate further in order to maintain export competivemess.
Dealers said this created havoc in a market already left short by a large import payment which went out last Wednesday.

On Monday, the local unit closed at 11.5200/6500 on the U.S. dollar from Friday's 11.4900/6000 but was firmer on sterling at 18.9320/9690 compared to 19.1990/20.3500 because of a stronger U.S. dollar overseas.
It was at 6.2440/2565 from 6.3125/3165 against the mark and at 2.5200/5275 versus the rand, slightly up from 2.5360/5395.
